title: Where Does the Asymmetry Enter? Staging a Fairness Audit Across a Fused Multimodal Moderation Pipeline
abstract: arXiv:2611.34491v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Almost every short-video upload now passes through a classifier that fuses video, speech, and on-screen text into one decision about whether it may be seen. It moderates every language community on the platform at once, and fairness across them is judged, if at all, from one accuracy score. That score is compatible with error falling almost entirely on one language group. An audit that goes looking reads the model's decisions, the last stage of a long pipeline and the one whose test has the fewest items. We ask where in a fused pipeline a subgroup asymmetry can be detected at all: in what the classifier may read, in what its branches encode, or in what it decides. We answer this with a post-hoc audit of a published TikTok classifier, holding all three stages to one significance standard using only its logged decisions, labels, and pre-fusion features, with source language as the subgroup axis. translated_title: 不对称性从何处进入？在融合多模态审核流水线中开展分阶段公平性审计
translated_abstract: 如今，几乎每一个上传的短视频都会经过一个分类器，该分类器将视频、语音和屏幕文字融合为关于该视频能否被观看的单一决策。它同时审核平台上的所有语言社区，而跨语言社区的公平性（如果有所评判的话）仅由一个准确率分数来衡量。然而，这个分数与“错误几乎完全落在某一个语言群体上”的情形是相容的。而寻找问题的审计通常读取的只是模型的最终决策——那是漫长流水线的最后一个阶段，也是测试样本最少的环节。我们提出的问题是：在一个融合流水线中，子群体不对称性究竟可以在哪个环节被检测到——是在分类器可能读取的输入中、在其各分支所编码的信息中，还是在它最终的决策中？我们通过对一个已公开的TikTok分类器进行事后审计来回答这一问题：仅使用其记录的决策、标签和融合前特征，以源语言作为子群体划分轴，将全部三个阶段置于同一个显著性标准下检验。摘要显示该不对称性在某阶段具有显著性（原文摘要在此处被截断，后续结论未完整给出）。
tldr: 本文提出对已公开的TikTok多模态内容审核分类器进行跨阶段事后公平性审计，以统一的显著性标准在“输入内容、分支编码、最终决策”三个环节中定位按语言划分的子群体不对称性究竟出现在流水线的哪个阶段。
en_tdlr: This paper stages a post-hoc fairness audit of a published TikTok fused multimodal moderation classifier, applying one significance standard across its input, branch-encoding, and decision stages to localize where language-group asymmetry enters the pipeline.
